en: 5. The Chapter on Truths (Saccayamaka) 5.1 The Section on Designations (Paṇṇattivāra) 5.1.2 The Exposition of the Section on Designations (Paṇṇattivāraniddesa)
5.1.2.1. Chapter on the Purification of Terms (Padasodhanavāra) 5.1.2.1.1.
Direct Order (Anuloma) Is suffering the truth of suffering? Yes.
Is the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) suffering (dukkha)?

With the exception of bodily suffering and mental suffering, the remainder of the truth of suffering is not suffering. Bodily suffering and mental suffering are both suffering and the truth of suffering.
Is the origin (samudaya) the truth of the origin (samudayasacca)?
Excluding the truth of origination (*samudayasacca*), the remainder is origination but not the truth of origination. The truth of origination is both origination and the truth of origination.
Is the truth of origination origination? Yes.
Is cessation (*nirodha*) the truth of cessation (*nirodhasacca*)?
Excluding the truth of cessation (*nirodhasacca*), the remainder is cessation, but not the truth of cessation. The truth of cessation is both cessation and the truth of cessation.
Is the truth of cessation cessation? Yes.
Is the path (*magga*) the truth of the path (*maggasacca*)?
With the exception of the truth of the path, the remainder is the path, but not the truth of the path. The truth of the path is both the path and the truth of the path.
Is the truth of the path the path? Yes.
5.1.2.1.2. Negative (Paccanīka)
Is it not suffering, yet not the truth of suffering?

With the exception of bodily suffering and mental suffering, the remainder is not suffering, but is the truth of suffering. With the exception of both suffering and the truth of suffering, the remainder is neither suffering nor the truth of suffering.
Is it not the truth of suffering, yet not suffering? Yes.
Is it not origination, yet not the truth of origination? Yes.
Is it not the truth of origination, yet not origination?

With the exception of the truth of origination, the remainder is not the truth of origination, but is origination. With the exception of both origination and the truth of origination, the remainder is neither origination nor the truth of origination.
Is it not cessation, and is it not the truth of cessation? Yes.
Is that which is not the truth of cessation not cessation?

With the exception of the truth of cessation, the remainder is not the truth of cessation, but it is cessation. With the exception of both cessation and the truth of cessation, the remainder is neither cessation nor the truth of cessation.
Is it not the path, yet not the truth of the path? Yes.
Is it not the truth of the path, yet not the path?

With the exception of the truth of the path, the remainder is neither the truth of the path nor the path. With the exception of both the path and the truth of the path, the remainder is neither the path nor the truth of the path.
5.1.2.2. The Wheel-Section Rooted in the Purification of Terms (Padasodhanamūlacakkavāra) 5.1.2.2.1.
Positive Order (Anuloma) Is suffering the truth of suffering? Yes.
Are all truths the truth of origination?
The truth of origination is both a truth and the truth of origination; the remaining truths are truths but not the truth of origination.
Is suffering the truth of suffering? Yes.
Are truths the truth of cessation? … [and so on] … Are truths the truth of the path?
The truth of the path is both a truth and the truth of the path. The remaining truths are truths but not the truth of the path.
Is origination the truth of origination?
Excluding the truth of origination (*samudayasacca*), the remainder is origination, but not the truth of origination. The truth of origination is both origination and the truth of origination.
Are all truths the truth of suffering (*dukkhasacca*)? … [as before] … Are all truths the truth of cessation (*nirodhasacca*)? … [as before] … Are all truths the truth of the path (*maggasacca*)?
The truth of the path is both a truth and the truth of the path. The remaining truths are truths, but not the truth of the path.
Is cessation the truth of cessation?
With the exception of the truth of cessation, the remainder is cessation but not the truth of cessation. The truth of cessation is both cessation and the truth of cessation.
Are the truths the truth of suffering? … [as above] … Are the truths the truth of origin? … [as above] … Are the truths the truth of the path?
The truth of the path is both a truth and the truth of the path. The remaining truths are truths but not the truth of the path.
Is the path the truth of the path?
With the exception of the truth of the path, the remainder is the path but not the truth of the path. The truth of the path is both the path and the truth of the path.
Are all truths the truth of suffering? … [and so on] … Are all truths the truth of origination? … [and so on] … Are all truths the truth of cessation?
The truth of cessation is both a truth and the truth of cessation. The remaining truths are truths but not the truth of cessation.
5.1.2.2.2. Negative (Paccanīka)
Is it not suffering, yet not the truth of suffering?

With the exception of bodily suffering and mental suffering, the remainder is not suffering, but is the truth of suffering. With the exception of both suffering and the truth of suffering, the remainder is neither suffering nor the truth of suffering.
Is it not the truths, yet not the truth of origination? Yes.
Is it not suffering, yet not the truth of suffering?

With the exception of bodily suffering and mental suffering, the remainder is not suffering, but is the truth of suffering. With the exception of both suffering and the truth of suffering, the remainder is neither suffering nor the truth of suffering.
Is it not the truths, yet not the truth of cessation? ... [as above] ... Is it not the truths, yet not the truth of the path? Yes.
Is it not origination, yet not the truth of origination? Yes.
Are they not truths, yet not the truth of suffering? Yes.
Is it not origination, yet not the truth of origination? Yes.
Are they not truths and not the truth of cessation? ... [etc. Are they not truths and not the truth of the path? Yes.
Is it not cessation and not the truth of cessation? Yes.
Are they not truths and not the truth of suffering? ... [etc. Are they not truths and not the truth of origin? ... [etc. Are they not truths and not the truth of the path? Yes.
Is it not the path and not the truth of the path? Yes.
Are they not truths and not the truth of suffering? Yes.
Is it not the path and not the truth of the path? Yes.
Are they not truths, yet not the truth of origin? ... pe ... Are they not truths, yet not the truth of cessation? Yes. 5.1.2.3.
Chapter on Pure Truths (Suddhasaccavāra) 5.1.2.3.1.
Positive Order (Anuloma)
Is it suffering that is a truth? Yes.
Are all truths the truth of suffering?
The truth of suffering is both a truth and the truth of suffering; the remaining truths are truths but not the truth of suffering.
Is the origin of suffering a truth? Yes.
… [and so on] … Is cessation a truth? Yes.
… [and so on] … Is the path a truth? Yes.
Are truths the truth of the path?
The truth of the path is both a truth and the truth of the path. The remaining truths are truths but not the truth of the path.
5.1.2.3.2. Negative (Paccanīka)
Is it not suffering and not truth?
With the exception of suffering, the remaining truths are not suffering, yet they are truths. With the exception of both suffering and truth, the remainder is neither suffering nor truths.
Is it not truths and not the truth of suffering? Yes.

5.1.2.4. The Wheel Chapter on the Pure Truth-Basis (Suddhasaccamūlacakkavāra)
5.1.2.4.1. In the forward order:
Is suffering a truth? Yes.
Are truths the truth of the origin? No.
The truth of the origin is both a truth and the truth of the origin. The remaining truths are truths but not the truth of the origin.
Is suffering a truth? Yes.
Are the truths the truth of cessation? ... [etc. ... Are the truths the truth of the path?
The Truth of the Path is both a truth and the Truth of the Path. The remaining truths are truths but not the Truth of the Path.
Is origination a truth? Yes.
… [as before] … Is cessation a truth? Yes. … [as before] …
Is the path a truth? Yes.
Are truths the truth of suffering? …pe… Are truths the truth of origin? …pe… Are truths the truth of cessation?
The truth of cessation is both a truth and the truth of cessation; the remaining truths are truths but not the truth of cessation.
5.1.2.4.2. Negative (Paccanīka) Is it not suffering and not a truth?
With the exception of suffering, the remaining truths are not suffering, yet they are truths. With the exception of both suffering and truths, the remainder are neither suffering nor truths.
Is it not the truth, yet not the truth of origination? Yes.
Is it not suffering, yet not the truth?
With the exception of suffering, the remaining truths are not suffering, but they are truths. With the exception of both suffering and the truth, the remainder are neither suffering nor truths.
Are they not truths, yet not the truth of cessation? …pe… Are they not truths, yet not the truth of the path? Yes.
Are they not origin, yet not truths?
With the exception of origin, the remaining truths are not origin, but are truths. With the exception of both origin and truth, the remainder are neither origin nor truths.
Is it not the truth, yet not the truth of suffering?
… [as before] … Is it not cessation, yet not the truth?
With the exception of cessation … [as before] …
Is it not the Path and not the Truths?
With the exception of the Path, the remaining Truths are not the Path, but they are Truths. With the exception of both the Path and the Truths, the remainder are neither the Path nor the Truths.
Are they not the Truths and not the Truth of Suffering? Yes.
Is it not the Path and not the Truths?
With the exception of the Path, the remaining Truths are not the Path, but they are Truths. With the exception of both the Path and the Truths, the remainder are neither the Path nor the Truths.
Is it not the Truths and not the Origin Truth? Yes. … [and so on] …
Is it not the truth, and not the truth of cessation? Yes, it is.
